The Rason Special Economic Zone is a 746 square kilometre zone in the far north-east of North Korea, on the Tumen River border with China and Russia. entries_new.story:
The Kaesong Industrial Region is a special administrative industrial region of North Korea, formed in 2002 from part of Kaesong city, ten kilometres north of the Korean Demilitarized Zone. Its industrial park, opened in December 2004, was run by a South Korean committee under a 50-year lease from 2004, with Hyundai Asan hired to develop the land. South Korean firms employed North Korean workers there: 123 companies employed about 53,000 North Korean workers and 800 South Korean staff as of April 2013.
North Korea withdrew its workers in April 2013 during a crisis, and the park reopened after an agreement that August. On 10 February 2016 South Korea's Ministry of Unification closed it, which it called temporary, after a North Korean satellite launch and claimed hydrogen bomb test. North Korea then expelled the South Korean workers and froze their assets. In 2017 President Moon Jae-in said he wanted to reopen and expand it.

The Dawei Special Economic Zone Law of 27 January 2011 gives investors income tax exemptions for their first five or seven years, customs relief, the right to hold foreign bank accounts, and a promise that the government will not seize or nationalise businesses there. entries_new.founder: Government of North Korea; Yang Bin
entries_new.stopped_by: Chinese authorities' arrest and imprisonment of chief executive designate Yang Bin
entries_new.passports: A separate passport was planned under the Basic Law
entries_new.laws: Basic Law of the Sinuiju SAR (2002)
entries_new.story:
The Sinuiju Special Administrative Region was a planned self-governing region of North Korea in the city of Sinuiju, on the border with China, proclaimed in 2002. North Korean officials first offered Chinese-Dutch businessman Yang Bin the post of director of a special economic zone there in 2001. Yang asked for a larger area of 82 square kilometres and for a special administrative region on the model of Hong Kong and Macau instead, with its own Basic Law, passport, flag and seal, and autonomy in all areas except foreign policy and defence. In 2002 the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly promulgated the Basic Law and named Yang chief executive.
Before he took office, Chinese authorities arrested Yang, and he was sentenced to 18 years in prison for tax evasion and other economic crimes. The project has been dormant since and was never put into operation.

entries_new.name: Mount Kumgang Tourist Region
entries_new.founder: Government of North Korea; Hyundai Asan
entries_new.challenge: North Korea seized South Korean properties in 2010 after South Korea suspended tours in 2008
entries_new.story:
The Mount Kumgang Tourist Region was a special administrative region of North Korea, separated from Kangwon Province in 2002 to handle South Korean tourists visiting Mount Kumgang. It covered 530 square kilometres. South Korea's Hyundai Asan held a 30-year exclusive deal to develop it and built much of its infrastructure, and over one million South Koreans visited from 1998 to July 2008.
South Korea suspended tours in July 2008 after South Korean tourist Park Wang-ja was shot and killed when, according to the North Korean government, she entered a military area. North Korea seized five South Korean-owned properties in April 2010 and began running tours itself. In January 2024 North Korea announced it would close the Mount Kumgang International Tourism Administration.
